ergo.description: The version of the spec the report follows

engine.description: What made the report. A report's hash leaves it out.

compliant.description: true when there's at least one requirement and none is not_met

subjects.description: The subjects the requirements use, directly or through the subjects they narrow or read from, by name.

description.description: The subject's description, or "" when it has none.

from.description: How the subject is found, as a from line is written, or <invalid from> when it is written wrong.

identified_by.description: The path of the subject's id, or null when it has none and the whole subject is its id.

parts.description: Every part the subject has, including the ones it keeps from a subject it narrows, by alias.

from.description: The part's path, written as a sentence writes it, or <invalid from> when it is written wrong.

identified_by.description: The path of the part's id, <invalid identified_by> when it is written wrong, or null when it has none.

causes.description: The causes of the rows that would be violations of the requirement, worst first, each with how many rows have it. Empty when the requirement is met or not_applicable.

checks.description: Each check as written, plus the checks Ergo adds, which start with $.

require.description: The require the requirement was written with, or every by default.

subject.description: The name of the subject the requirement checks, or null when it names none or one that isn't in the policy's subjects.

locations.description: Where the value was read, as JSON Pointers from the root of the input, or $params: and a pointer from the root of the params. Empty when no location could be given.

part.description: Present when the input was read through a part: the part's alias as the check writes it, and the id read inside the part, or null.

type.description: The name of the requirement's subject.

id.description: The subject's id, or null for the rows of the checks Ergo adds to a requirement.

in.description: Only for a child subject: the name and id of each subject it was read from, its parent and, three subjects deep, its grandparent.

failed_items.description: Only on rows of every, some and for checks, on the $applies row of a subject whose from line has one condition, a some or an every, and on the $min_subjects row of a subject whose from line has every.

item.description: The list item the entry belongs to, like item 2 of tests. For a list that failed while walking, the same as path.

failed_assertions.description: Only on entries of for checks: the sentences that failed for that item, in the order written.

failed_items.description: Only on entries of for checks with two items, when the second item failed for that item before any sentence was checked: those failures, in path order.

failed_assertions.description: Only on rows of checks written as several sentences without a for line, and on the $applies row of a subject whose from line has several conditions: the ones that failed, in the order written.

inputs.description: Only on a sentence that has no items: what it read for that item, as the entries of a check row's inputs, with the alias names as the sentence writes them.

items.description: Only on entries of for checks with two items, for a sentence that reads the second item's alias: the items of the second list the sentence failed for, in path order.

inputs.description: What the sentence read for that pair of items, as the entries of a check row's inputs, with the alias names as the sentence writes them.

items.description: Only on entries of for checks with two items, for a sentence that reads the second item's alias: the items of the second list the sentence failed for, in path order.
